learningObjective: Reason about warp granularity: 32-thread SIMT execution unit with per-lane predication for divergence.

canonicalClaims.claim: On all NVIDIA CUDA GPUs, a warp is 32 threads (`warpSize == 32`), scheduled as one instruction issue unit; all 32 lanes execute the same instruction with per-lane predication handling divergence.
conditions: NVIDIA architecture as documented since Kepler.
nonImplications: Does not imply divergence is always harmful; whole-warp branches are free.
Does not imply lockstep at every micro-op on Volta+ (Independent Thread Scheduling).

misconceptions.claim: Warp size varies across NVIDIA generations.
misconceptions.whyWrong: warpSize has always been 32 on NVIDIA CUDA GPUs.

misconceptions.claim: Warps are a software-only abstraction with no hardware backing.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Warp scheduler is a real hardware unit; warp primitives use real hardware ops.

misconceptions.claim: SIMT means threads in a warp execute one at a time, round-robin.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Threads execute in parallel per issued instruction.

misconceptions.claim: Warp size is 64 on AMD, so NVIDIA is likely to move to 64.
misconceptions.whyWrong: AMD's wavefront is 64 or 32 depending on gen; NVIDIA has kept warp=32 across generations.

implementationFacts: Volta+ Independent Thread Scheduling allows divergent lanes to maintain independent program counters.
Modern SMs have 4 warp schedulers each issuing one warp instruction per cycle.
